title: A simple start with a gradual learning curve, or high difficulty right from minute one? What do you prefer in a tactical/card game?
author: VaurensBeastBorn
selftext:
Hey everyone!

We’ve been playtesting our turn-based card game with friends, and their feedback triggered a huge debate in our team about how to structure the early game:

* **Option A: Simple start & gradual progression.** Basic card effects and clean mechanics at the beginning. Easy to pick up, with complexity, synergies, and denser card text introduced over time.
* **Option B: Dense & deep right away.** Complex cards that do multiple things right from turn one, forcing a steeper learning curve from minute one.

When you play a new tactical card game, do you prefer a smooth entry that builds up gradually, or do you like rich, multi-layered card mechanics straight out of the gate, even if it feels a bit overwhelming at first?

I’d love to hear your thoughts and what usually keeps you hooked!

comments.author: Hiroshi_S
comments.body:
I'd lean towards A, but not because tactical games should be easy. The depth is the whole point. It's just that people can only enjoy complex interactions once they understand the pieces, the same way maths starts with addition. A steep start doesn't make a game deeper, it just means fewer people ever reach the deep part.

I ran into the same question with my own game, a cinema scheduling sim. The standard run is 50 weeks, but I also added a 20-week run so new players can see the whole loop, start to finish, in one short session. Same rules, just a shorter run, so learning them costs less.

Maybe there's a middle ground for you too: keep the dense cards, but hold them back for the first few fights, so the first multi-effect card feels like a reward instead of a wall.
